cohorts.name: Acute Inflammatory / Infective Response
cohorts.description: Neutrophil-predominant leucocytosis with raised acute-phase proteins - the systemic response to bacterial infection or acute inflammation.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference Sepsis row spans Infectious Diseases and Inflammation and names 'CBC (WBC), CRP/inflammatory markers if available, blood culture' - three profiles in one marker set.

triggers.label: Procalcitonin at or above 0.5 ng/mL - suggests bacterial infection

supporting.label: Ferritin markedly raised as an acute-phase reactant

evidence.citation: Singer M et al., The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3), JAMA 2016;315:801-10
evidence.note: Sepsis is organ dysfunction from a dysregulated host response; laboratory markers support but do not define it.

evidence.citation: Wacker C et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2013;13:426-35
evidence.note: Procalcitonin discriminates bacterial sepsis from non-infectious systemic inflammation.

diseases.name: Reactive Leukocytosis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated WBC with a clear infectious/inflammatory trigger and normal differential pattern'; Related Markers/Tests: WBC count and differential
diseases.requires_any_basis: Disease Master Definition: 'An elevated white blood cell count occurring as a normal immune response'. The condition IS a raised WBC, so it is credited only when the WBC trigger itself fired - a raised CRP or procalcitonin with a normal or unmeasured WBC is not leukocytosis.

diseases.name: Sepsis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly abnormal WBC (very high or very low) with fever/hypotension and suspected infection source'; Related Markers/Tests: CBC (WBC), CRP/inflammatory markers, blood culture. Weight held moderate because fever and hypotension are not lab-derivable.
diseases.requires_any_basis: Disease Master High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly abnormal WBC ... with suspected infection source'; Related Markers/Tests: CBC (WBC), blood culture. Procalcitonin is admitted because this cluster already cites Wacker 2013 for it as a sepsis marker. A raised CRP on its own is none of these and does not credit sepsis.

diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked as a common source; confirmed only by the urinary markers in the UTI cohort

cohorts.name: Severe Systemic Infection Pattern
cohorts.description: Markedly deranged white cell count - very high or very low - with high procalcitonin or a positive blood culture. A time-critical combination.

triggers.label: WBC below 4000 /uL - leukopenia in the context of infection

evidence.citation: Singer M et al., JAMA 2016;315:801-10
evidence.note: Sepsis-3: SOFA-based organ dysfunction criteria including platelets, bilirubin, creatinine and coagulation.

evidence.citation: Evans L et al., Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines 2021, Crit Care Med 2021;49:e1063-e1143
evidence.note: Time-critical recognition and treatment of sepsis.

diseases.name: Sepsis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly abnormal WBC (very high or very low) with fever/hypotension and suspected infection source'; Related Markers/Tests: CBC (WBC), CRP/inflammatory markers if available, blood culture

diseases.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators name 'a critically ill patient'; DIC is a recognised complication of severe sepsis

diseases.name: Leukemia (Suspected/Screening)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly abnormal WBC count (very high or low) with abnormal differential' - the haematological alternative to infection

cohorts.name: Chronic Inflammatory Signal
cohorts.description: Persistent acute-phase elevation without a neutrophil-predominant leucocytosis - the pattern seen in autoimmune and chronic inflammatory disease.

triggers.label: CRP raised but not in the acute bacterial range

supporting.label: White cell count normal - argues against acute bacterial infection
Anaemia - consistent with anaemia of chronic disease
Ferritin raised as an acute-phase reactant
Monocytes raised - seen in chronic infection and inflammatory disease

evidence.citation: Weiss G, Ganz T, Goodnough LT, Blood 2019;133:40-50
evidence.note: Anaemia of inflammation: hepcidin-mediated iron restriction with raised inflammatory markers.

evidence.citation: Bray C et al., WMJ 2016;115:317-21
evidence.note: ESR and CRP: complementary acute-phase markers with different kinetics.

diseases.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'RA factor (quantitative), ASO (quantitative, if used for differential)'; inflammatory markers support but do not establish the diagnosis

diseases.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: ANA, Anti-dsDNA, CBC, Urinalysis

diseases.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's Disease/Ulcerative Colitis)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'Stool analysis (occult blood), CBC, inflammatory markers'

diseases.name: Tuberculosis
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'Sputum/urine analysis where relevant, inflammatory markers'

cohorts.name: Atopic / Allergic Sensitisation Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised total or allergen-specific IgE with eosinophilia - the laboratory signature of atopy. Which allergic condition it manifests as depends on symptoms, not on the blood test.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Eosinophil counts come from Blood Counts while IgE comes from the Allergy Panel; the two together are far more informative than either alone.

triggers.label: Allergen-specific IgE at or above 0.35 kUA/L - sensitisation present
Total IgE at or above 100 IU/mL
Absolute eosinophil count at or above 500 /uL

supporting.label: Thyroid antibodies raised - the Disease Master notes this autoimmune association for chronic urticaria

evidence.citation: Bousquet J et al., ARIA 2019 update, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2020;145:70-80
evidence.note: Allergen-specific IgE sensitisation must be interpreted alongside symptom history; sensitisation alone is not allergy.

evidence.citation: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) 2023 Report
evidence.note: Allergic (atopic) asthma phenotype defined by sensitisation plus compatible respiratory symptoms.

evidence.citation: Valent P et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2012;130:607-12
evidence.note: Absolute eosinophil count thresholds for eosinophilia and hypereosinophilia.

diseases.name: Allergic Rhinitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated specific IgE to common inhalant allergens with matching symptom pattern'; Related Markers/Tests: Specific IgE panel for common inhalant allergens

diseases.name: Allergic Asthma
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated specific IgE to common triggers with recurrent wheeze/breathlessness'; Related Markers/Tests: Specific IgE panel, Total IgE

diseases.name: Atopic Dermatitis/Eczema
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated total/specific IgE with characteristic chronic itchy rash pattern'; Related Markers/Tests: Total IgE

diseases.name: Allergic Conjunctivitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated specific IgE to inhalant allergens with matching eye symptoms'

diseases.name: Food Allergy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated specific IgE to a food allergen with a clear history of reaction on exposure'

diseases.name: Chronic Urticaria
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'Total IgE; specific IgE panel if a trigger is suspected; thyroid antibodies (autoimmune association)'

diseases.name: Drug Allergy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators rest on 'Clear temporal relationship between drug exposure and reaction onset' - not lab-derivable

diseases.name: Insect Sting Allergy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'History of a systemic reaction to a sting, or elevated venom-specific IgE'

diseases.name: Anaphylaxis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Any history of a rapid multi-system reaction' - a clinical event, not a screening finding

cohorts.name: Marked Eosinophilia
cohorts.description: Eosinophils substantially raised. In addition to atopy, parasitic infection and drug reactions are important causes.

triggers.label: Absolute eosinophil count at or above 1500 /uL - hypereosinophilia
Eosinophils at or above 12% of the differential

supporting.label: Ova, cysts or parasites seen on stool microscopy

evidence.citation: Valent P et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2012;130:607-12
evidence.note: Consensus definitions of eosinophilia and hypereosinophilia and their diagnostic workup.

evidence.citation: O'Connell EM, Nutman TB, Semin Hematol 2012;49:149-59
evidence.note: Helminth infection as a leading global cause of eosinophilia.

diseases.name: Intestinal Parasitic Infection
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Ova, cysts, or parasites identified on stool microscopy, especially with compatible symptoms or exposure history'; Related Markers/Tests: Stool microscopy/ova and parasite exam

diseases.name: Allergic Asthma
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: Specific IgE panel for inhalant allergens; Total IgE

diseases.name: Atopic Dermatitis/Eczema
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: Total IgE

cohorts.name: Autoimmune Serology Pattern
cohorts.description: Positive autoantibodies with inflammatory markers. The specific autoantibody, not the ANA alone, determines which condition is most likely.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference tags Rheumatoid Arthritis and Psoriatic Arthritis to both Arthritis Screening and Autoimmune Disorders, so serology and inflammatory markers are pooled across those profiles.

triggers.label: Anti-CCP antibody raised - highly specific for rheumatoid arthritis

supporting.label: Anaemia - common in active connective tissue disease
Thrombocytopenia - a haematological feature of lupus
Leukopenia - a haematological feature of lupus
ASO raised - used in the Disease Master for the RA differential

evidence.citation: Aringer M et al., 2019 EULAR/ACR Classification Criteria for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Arthritis Rheumatol 2019;71:1400-12
evidence.note: Positive ANA is the entry criterion; organ-specific and immunological domains score toward classification.

evidence.citation: Aletaha D et al., 2010 ACR/EULAR Rheumatoid Arthritis Classification Criteria, Arthritis Rheum 2010;62:2569-81
evidence.note: RF and anti-CCP with acute-phase reactants and joint involvement form the classification score.

evidence.citation: Shiboski CH et al., 2016 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Primary Sjogren's Syndrome, Arthritis Rheumatol 2017;69:35-45
evidence.note: Anti-SSA/Ro with objective dryness measures; ANA and RF are frequent co-findings.

diseases.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated RA factor with typical symmetric joint symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: RA factor (quantitative), ASO

diseases.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive ANA with multi-system symptoms (joint, skin, renal, hematologic)'; Related Markers/Tests: ANA, Anti-dsDNA, CBC, Urinalysis

diseases.name: Sjögren's Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive ANA/RA factor with characteristic dry eye and dry mouth symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: ANA, RA factor

diseases.name: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive ANA with overlapping lupus/scleroderma/myositis-like symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: ANA, RA factor

diseases.name: ANCA-Associated Vasculitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive ANCA with abnormal urinalysis (blood/protein) and elevated creatinine'

diseases.name: Autoimmune Hepatitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated liver enzymes with positive ANA and elevated globulin'

diseases.name: Psoriatic Arthritis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Joint symptoms with an existing or family history of psoriasis, and a negative RA factor' - a seronegative pattern

diseases.name: Autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto's)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Profile(s) includes Autoimmune Disorders; thyroid autoimmunity commonly coexists with other autoimmune disease

cohorts.name: Coeliac Serology Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised tissue transglutaminase IgA, interpreted alongside total IgA because selective IgA deficiency makes the test falsely negative.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Total IgA from the Immunity profile is required to validate the tTG-IgA result - a cross-profile dependency the clinical reference captures by listing both markers on the Celiac Disease row.

supporting.label: Total IgA low - the tTG-IgA result may be falsely negative and IgG-based testing is needed
Iron stores depleted - unexplained iron deficiency is a classic presentation

evidence.citation: Rubio-Tapia A et al., ACG Clinical Guidelines: Diagnosis and Management of Celiac Disease, Am J Gastroenterol 2023;118:59-76
evidence.note: tTG-IgA with total IgA as first-line serology; duodenal biopsy on a gluten-containing diet for confirmation in adults.

evidence.citation: Husby S et al., ESPGHAN Guidelines for Diagnosing Coeliac Disease 2020, J Pediatr Gastroenterol Nutr 2020;70:141-56
evidence.note: The role of tTG-IgA titre magnitude and the need to exclude IgA deficiency.

diseases.name: Celiac Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated tTG-IgA with compatible symptoms or unexplained iron/folate deficiency'; Related Markers/Tests: Anti-tTG IgA, Total IgA

diseases.name: Malabsorption Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Chronic diarrhea with steatorrhea plus multiple vitamin/mineral deficiencies'

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked because coeliac disease is a leading cause of iron deficiency that does not respond to oral iron

diseases.name: Selective IgA Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low serum IgA with normal other immunoglobulins' - relevant here because it invalidates IgA-based coeliac serology

cohorts.name: Antibody Deficiency Pattern
cohorts.description: One or more immunoglobulin classes below range, which predisposes to recurrent bacterial infection.

evidence.citation: Bonilla FA et al., Practice Parameter for the Diagnosis and Management of Primary Immunodeficiency, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2015;136:1186-205
evidence.note: Diagnostic criteria for CVID (reduced IgG with reduced IgA or IgM plus impaired vaccine responses) and selective IgA deficiency.

evidence.citation: Yazdani R et al., J Investig Allergol Clin Immunol 2020;30:14-34
evidence.note: Selective IgA deficiency: isolated low IgA with normal IgG and IgM.

diseases.name: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low IgG with low IgA and/or IgM and history of recurrent infections'; Related Markers/Tests: Immunoglobulin IgA/IgG/IgM (Serum)

diseases.name: Selective IgA Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low serum IgA with normal other immunoglobulins'; Related Markers/Tests: Immunoglobulin IgA (Serum)

cohorts.name: HIV Screening and Immune Status
cohorts.description: A reactive HIV screen, or a low CD4 count reflecting the degree of immunosuppression in someone already known to be positive.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference carries two rows - HIV under STD Profile/Blood Counts for detection, and HIV/AIDS Immune Status Monitoring under Immunity/STD Profile for CD4-based staging. This cohort feeds both.

supporting.label: CD4 count below 200 cells/uL - advanced immunosuppression

evidence.citation: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Testing Services, 2019
evidence.note: A reactive screening test requires confirmation by a second assay before any diagnosis is communicated.

evidence.citation: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Prevention, Testing, Treatment, 2021
evidence.note: CD4 <200 cells/uL defines advanced HIV disease with need for opportunistic infection prophylaxis.

diseases.name: HIV
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Reactive HIV screening test confirmed by a second confirmatory method'; Related Markers/Tests: HIV antibody/antigen test; CBC used only as a general cross-reference. Weight reflects that a screen alone is not diagnostic.

diseases.name: HIV/AIDS - Immune Status Monitoring
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low CD4 count in a confirmed HIV-positive individual signals advancing immunosuppression'; Related Markers/Tests: CD4, CD4/CD8 ratio, CD3, Natural Killer Cells

cohorts.name: Sexually Transmitted Infection Screen
cohorts.description: A positive result on one or more sexually transmitted infection tests.

supporting.label: Treponemal test positive - confirms the non-treponemal screen
HIV screen reactive - co-infection is common
HBsAg positive - hepatitis B is sexually transmissible

evidence.citation: Workowski KA et al., CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines 2021, MMWR Recomm Rep 2021;70(4):1-187
evidence.note: NAAT as the diagnostic standard for chlamydia and gonorrhoea; reverse/traditional syphilis testing algorithms.

evidence.citation: WHO Guidelines for the Management of Symptomatic Sexually Transmitted Infections, 2021
evidence.note: Partner notification and co-infection screening as standard practice on any positive result.

diseases.name: Syphilis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Reactive VDRL/RPR confirmed by treponemal test'; Related Markers/Tests: VDRL/RPR (screening)

diseases.name: Chlamydia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive NAAT/PCR result'; Related Markers/Tests: Chlamydia NAAT/PCR or antigen test

diseases.name: Gonorrhea
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive NAAT/PCR or culture result'; Related Markers/Tests: Gonorrhea NAAT/PCR or culture

diseases.name: Herpes Simplex (Type I & II)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive HSV-2 IgG (genital association) or recurrent symptomatic outbreaks'; Related Markers/Tests: HSV IgG/IgM serology

diseases.name: HIV
diseases.dm_basis: Related Profile(s): STD Profile - co-infection screening is standard on any positive STI result

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.dm_basis: Related Profile(s) on the Hepatitis B row includes STD Profile

cohorts.name: Viral Hepatitis Serology
cohorts.description: A positive hepatitis marker, interpreted alongside the liver enzymes.

triggers.label: Anti-HAV IgM positive - acute hepatitis A

supporting.label: INR prolonged - a marker of severe hepatic impairment
AFP raised - hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance marker in chronic hepatitis

evidence.citation: WHO Guidelines on Hepatitis B and C Testing, 2017
evidence.note: HBsAg and anti-HCV as the primary serological screening markers, with nucleic acid testing for confirmation of active HCV infection.

evidence.citation: Terrault NA et al., AASLD 2018 Hepatitis B Guidance, Hepatology 2018;67:1560-99
evidence.note: HBsAg with ALT and viral load determines phase of infection and need for treatment.

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive HBsAg with elevated liver enzymes'; Related Markers/Tests: HBsAg, Liver function markers (SGOT, SGPT)

diseases.name: Hepatitis C
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive Anti-HCV with elevated liver enzymes'

diseases.name: Hepatitis A
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly elevated SGOT/SGPT with jaundice and positive Anti-HAV IgM'

diseases.name: Liver Cancer (Hepatocellular Carcinoma)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Rising or markedly elevated AFP in a patient with chronic liver disease'; chronic hepatitis B/C is the leading risk factor

diseases.name: Liver-related Coagulopathy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/INR with abnormal LFTs'

cohorts.name: Acute Febrile Tropical Illness Panel
cohorts.description: A positive result on one of the acute febrile illness tests, interpreted with the blood count changes that accompany these infections.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference itself tags Typhoid Fever to three profiles and Dengue Fever to two, and the Data Quality Notes sheet recommends multi-profile tagging for exactly these rows. Blood Counts parameters are pooled in because platelet and haematocrit changes are named in the Dengue High-Risk Indicators.

supporting.label: Thrombocytopenia - characteristic of dengue, malaria and scrub typhus
Rising haematocrit - plasma leakage warning sign in dengue
Leukopenia - typical of dengue and typhoid
Blood culture positive - confirms enteric fever
Bilirubin raised - jaundice, seen in severe leptospirosis and malaria
Dengue IgG positive - with a positive IgM this suggests secondary infection, which carries a higher risk of severe dengue

evidence.citation: WHO, Dengue Guidelines for Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention and Control, 2009
evidence.note: NS1 antigen and IgM for diagnosis; falling platelets with rising haematocrit are warning signs of severe dengue.

evidence.citation: WHO Guidelines for Malaria, 2023
evidence.note: Rapid diagnostic test or microscopy for confirmation before treatment.

evidence.citation: Parry CM et al., N Engl J Med 2002;347:1770-82
evidence.note: Blood culture is the diagnostic standard for typhoid; the Widal test has limited specificity and requires paired titres.

evidence.citation: Haake DA, Levett PN, Curr Top Microbiol Immunol 2015;387:65-97
evidence.note: Leptospirosis: IgM serology with the clinical triad of fever, myalgia and jaundice.

diseases.name: Dengue Fever
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive NS1/IgM with falling platelet count and rising hematocrit'; Related Markers/Tests: Dengue NS1 antigen, Dengue IgM/IgG, Platelet count

diseases.name: Malaria
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive blood smear/antigen test, especially with high parasite density'; Related Markers/Tests: Malaria antigen test, peripheral blood smear

diseases.name: Typhoid Fever
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Sustained fever with positive blood culture or a significantly rising Widal titer'. Weight reflects the Widal test's limited specificity noted in the same row.

diseases.name: Leptospirosis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive serology with fever, muscle pain, and jaundice, especially after flood/water exposure'

diseases.name: Scrub Typhus
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive serology with fever and an eschar following outdoor/rural exposure'

diseases.name: Brucellosis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive serology with recurring fever and relevant animal/dairy exposure'

diseases.name: Sepsis
diseases.dm_basis: Possible Complications across these infection rows include progression to severe systemic illness

cohorts.name: COVID-19 Test Result
cohorts.description: A positive SARS-CoV-2 test, or antibody evidence of past infection.

triggers.label: SARS-CoV-2 antibody positive - documents past infection or vaccination

supporting.label: D-dimer raised - thrombotic risk marker in COVID-19

evidence.citation: WHO, Diagnostic Testing for SARS-CoV-2, Interim Guidance 2020
evidence.note: RT-PCR as the reference standard; antigen tests are less sensitive but useful with high viral load.

evidence.citation: Soriano JB et al., WHO Clinical Case Definition of Post COVID-19 Condition, Lancet Infect Dis 2022;22:e102-e107
evidence.note: Symptoms persisting beyond 12 weeks with no alternative explanation.

diseases.name: COVID-19 (Acute Infection)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive RT-PCR/antigen test; low Ct value can suggest higher viral load'; Related Markers/Tests: COVID RT-PCR, COVID Antigen

diseases.name: Post-COVID/Long COVID Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistent multi-system symptoms beyond 12 weeks following confirmed/suspected COVID-19'; Related Markers/Tests: COVID Antibody. Weight is low because the defining feature is symptom duration, not a lab result.

cohorts.name: Varicella Zoster Immunity
cohorts.description: Varicella zoster IgG, which documents past infection or vaccination rather than acute disease.

triggers.label: Varicella zoster IgG positive - past infection or vaccination

evidence.citation: Marin M et al., CDC Prevention of Varicella Recommendations, MMWR Recomm Rep 2007;56(RR-4):1-40
evidence.note: VZV IgG documents immunity; acute varicella and zoster are clinical diagnoses.

diseases.name: Varicella (Chickenpox)/Herpes Zoster (Shingles)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive IgG indicates past infection/immunity; acute diagnosis is primarily clinical'. Weight is deliberately low - the Disease Master states this marker does not establish acute disease.

cohorts.name: Helicobacter pylori Infection Pattern
cohorts.description: A positive H. pylori test. Stool antigen and urea breath test indicate active infection; serology cannot distinguish current from past infection.

triggers.label: H. pylori stool antigen positive - active infection
Urea breath test positive - active infection
H. pylori antibody positive - cannot distinguish current from past infection

supporting.label: Iron stores depleted - H. pylori is a recognised cause of refractory iron deficiency
Faecal occult blood positive - possible ulcer bleeding
B12 low - atrophic gastritis impairs absorption

evidence.citation: Malfertheiner P et al., Maastricht VI/Florence Consensus Report, Gut 2022;71:1724-62
evidence.note: Urea breath test and stool antigen as non-invasive tests of active infection; serology cannot confirm current infection.

evidence.citation: Chey WD et al., ACG Clinical Guideline: Treatment of Helicobacter pylori Infection, Am J Gastroenterol 2017;112:212-39
evidence.note: Test-and-treat strategy and the association with peptic ulcer disease.

diseases.name: H. pylori Infection
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive stool antigen/breath test with symptomatic peptic ulcer disease'; Related Markers/Tests: H. pylori antigen (stool) or antibody test

diseases.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease/Gastritis (H. pylori-associated)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive Urea Breath Test or stool antigen with matching GI symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Helicobacter Pylori Abs (IgG/IgM), Helicobacter Antigen in Stool

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked because H. pylori is a recognised cause of iron deficiency refractory to oral supplementation

cohorts.name: Urinary Tract Infection Pattern
cohorts.description: Nitrite and leukocyte esterase positive with pyuria, ideally confirmed on culture.

triggers.label: Pus cells above 5 per high power field - pyuria

supporting.label: Systemic leucocytosis - possible upper tract involvement

evidence.citation: Gupta K et al., IDSA/ESCMID Guidelines for Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis and Pyelonephritis, Clin Infect Dis 2011;52:e103-20
evidence.note: Dipstick nitrite and leukocyte esterase with pyuria; culture for confirmation and susceptibility.

evidence.citation: Bonkat G et al., EAU Guidelines on Urological Infections, 2023
evidence.note: Diagnostic thresholds and the distinction between asymptomatic bacteriuria and infection.

diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive nitrite/leukocyte esterase with pyuria and a positive urine culture'; Related Markers/Tests: Leukocytes (urine), Nitrite (urine), Pus Cells, Urine culture

diseases.name: Sepsis
diseases.dm_basis: Possible Complications on the UTI row include ascending infection and systemic sepsis
